reason: Holds. The archive.org full-text index (search-inside across items) returns the Candles in Babylon scan (candlesinbabylon00leve) reading 'But we have only begun / to love the earth.' 'We have only begun / to imagine the fulness of life.' 'How could we tire of hope? / —so much is in bud.' In that OCR, single spaces mark line breaks (the same pattern splits the known 'unfolding that must / complete its gesture'), so the lineation with lower case line heads is the book's. The spelling is fulness with one l in Candles, Poems 1972-1982 (2001), Selected Poems (2002), New Selected Poems (2003) and Collected Poems (2013). The fullness spelling found in Greene's biography and in many reprints is the drift, not the text. The em dash before so much is Levertov's own, inside the quotation, which is allowed; the source and note carry none. shipped.js is clean: Levertov 0 of 3, not banned, no near match. Published 1982, and on hope. The source is 109 characters. One small correction: the four Swinburne lines (Garden of Proserpine) are set as the poem's own opening stanza, inside quotation marks (the Peace Book reprint shows the closing quotation mark after sea), not as a separate epigraph. So 'the Swinburne quotation' is more accurate than 'epigraph'. The betterCitation keeps the rest.
